actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The README installs MuJoCo with pip3 and starts the simulation with roslaunch humanoid_controllers load_cheat_controller.launch.
The README says the OCS2 controller is a separate monorepo build and must be compiled with catkin before the simulation is started.
The MJCF names the model humanoid_legged_description.
The model sets timestep 0.001 seconds, the PGS solver, gravity 0 0 -9.81 and twenty noslip iterations.
The base_link body carries a free joint, so the model has a floating base.

The leg hinge joints have limited ranges: leg_l1 -0.2 to 1.5708 and leg_r1 -1.5708 to 0.2; leg_l2, leg_l3, leg_r2 and leg_r3 -1.5708 to 1.5708; leg_l4 and leg_r4 0 to 2.356; leg_l5 and leg_r5 -0.8 to 0.8; and leg_l6 and leg_r6 -0.5236 to 0.5236.

The actuator block declares twelve motor actuators with gear 1 and explicit ctrlrange bounds: +/-150 for leg_l1, leg_l2, leg_r1 and leg_r2; +/-200 for leg_l3, leg_l4, leg_r3 and leg_r4; and +/-90 for leg_l5, leg_l6, leg_r5 and leg_r6.
The upstream MuJoCo loop computes data.ctrl from targetTorque, targetKp, targetPos, targetKd, targetVel and the last twelve qpos/qvel entries, then calls mj_step.
The upstream simulator sets sim_rate to 1000 and only steps when the wall-clock epoch has reached 1/sim_rate.
The upstream simulator publishes /jointsPosVel at 500 Hz from the last twelve qpos and qvel entries.
The upstream simulator initializes the base at [0, 0, 1.225] and the leg joints at the init_joint_pos values, then writes them into data.qpos.
The humanoid controller subscribes to /jointsPosVel and /imu and advertises /targetTorque, /targetPos, /targetVel, /targetKp and /targetKd.
The cheat controller node subscribes to pauseFlag and calls controller.update at 500 Hz unless the flag is set.
MuJoCoBase publishes /pauseFlag, toggles pause_flag on SPACE and resets the data with mj_resetData on BACKSPACE.

gaps: the fake backend is an analytic stand-in for the mujoco module, not a recording and not MuJoCo: it reads the same MJCF for the actuator count, ctrlrange and joint dimensions, but its step is a placeholder first-order motion of each leg joint toward its control value
the fake loads no mesh, texture, material or inertia and resolves no contact, friction, tendon, equality or sensor quantity; the real MuJoCo step is not represented
the fake's qpos/qvel integration and its initial free-joint quaternion are placeholder test data; no trajectory was compared with the real engine or the upstream simulator
the bridge reset does not reproduce the upstream simulator's manual initial pose, and no seed controls MuJoCo's internal state or any random number generator
the package does not run the upstream OCS2 gait/NMPC controller, WBC, state estimator, gait command publisher or ROS 1 nodes; it serves only the low-level model world
the upstream simulator sets a non-default start pose (base z 1.225 and init_joint_pos); the bridge reset restores the MJCF defaults instead, and the model has no keyframe
the model's arms, head and waist are visual meshes on the base body with no joints or actuators; only the twelve leg motor channels are controllable
no viewer, camera, image, ROS graph or rosbridge endpoint is exposed; the package is not a substitute for the upstream ROS controller stack
no physical humanoid is modelled or controlled; there is no hardware backend and no hardware run was performed

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: after an e-stop no step or reset is accepted until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch, and the model state stays readable
